name: Electronic voting and vote counting
definition: Votes cast or counted by electrical or computer machines, with totals reported automatically.
what: Seven US counties switched to punched-card voting with computer tallying for the 1964 presidential election.

sources.title: Electronic voting
sources.quote: Their first widespread use was in the US where 7 counties switched to this method for the 1964 presidential election.

note: The Voting machine article dates the Votomatic's first major success to 1965; the Electronic voting article says 1964. Earlier small-scale uses may exist.

name: Electronic voting and vote counting
definition: Votes cast or counted by electrical or computer machines, with totals reported automatically.
what: By the 1996 US presidential election punched-card systems with computer tabulation were used by over a third of registered US voters.

sources.title: Voting machine
sources.quote: By the 1996 Presidential election, some variation of the punched card system was used by 37.3% of registered voters in the United States.

note: US-only figure; the share may have exceeded this or been similar earlier. Brazil and India adopted DRE machines nationally later.

name: Electronic location tracking of people
definition: Worn tags, implants or devices that report where a person or vehicle is to a monitoring system.
what: Harvard researchers (the Schwitzgebel brothers) developed portable transceivers that recorded the location of volunteers.

sources.title: Electronic tagging
sources.quote: Portable transceivers that could record the location of volunteers were first developed by a group of researchers at Harvard University in the early 1960s.

note: Source gives only 'early 1960s'; 1962 is a midpoint, not a sourced year. The first pass said 1964, unverified. Vehicle-tracking and animal/astronaut telemetry were not examined.

name: Electronic location tracking of people
definition: Worn tags, implants or devices that report where a person or vehicle is to a monitoring system.
what: Judge Jack Love persuaded Michael Goss to found NIMCOS, which built radio ankle transmitters used to monitor offenders from a telephone-linked receiver.

sources.title: Electronic tagging
sources.quote: in 1982, an Arizona state district judge, Jack Love, convinced a former sales representative of Honeywell Information Systems, Michael T. Goss

note: The page gives 1982 for the company; the first pass said the first tagged probationer was in April 1983 (New Mexico), which I could not source. The Schwitzgebel 1960s system was a research use with volunteers.

name: Machine-readable identity and access card
definition: A card, disc or token encoded with a person's identity that machines read to grant access or check identity.
what: IBM developed a way of attaching magnetic stripes to plastic cards under a US government contract for a security system.

sources.title: Magnetic stripe card
sources.quote: In 1960, IBM built upon the magnetic tape idea and developed a reliable way of securing magnetic stripes to plastic cards

note: The same article says Forrest Parry had the idea in 1969, so 1960 conflicts with it. Punched-card key systems and earlier access cards were not checked.

name: Machine-readable identity and access card
definition: A card, disc or token encoded with a person's identity that machines read to grant access or check identity.
what: Tor Sornes's recodable punched plastic keycard lock, the VingCard, was used in hotels.

sources.title: Keycard lock
sources.quote: Tor Sørnes was credited with the invention in the 1970s.

note: Page gives only the 1970s; 1975 is from the first pass (single source). Hand-geometry Identimat with a magnetic-card reader (1970s) and 1960s card-access systems (e.g. Cardkey) may be earlier but were not sourced.

name: Automated fingerprint recognition
definition: A machine that identifies or authenticates a person by automatically reading and matching fingerprints.
what: J. H. Wegstein at the US National Bureau of Standards developed computer models of fingerprints to automate their analysis, leading to AFIS.

sources.title: Identix Incorporated
sources.quote: In the 1960s, J. H. Wegstein at the National Bureau of Standards developed computer models for fingerprint representations

note: Source gives only 'the 1960s'; 1965 is a midpoint, not sourced. Identimat is hand geometry, so rejected. Search results indicate the FBI asked NBS for help in 1963 and Rockwell built card readers from 1974, but I could not fetch these. 1999 IAFIS is a database, not the earliest.

name: Automated fingerprint recognition
definition: A machine that identifies or authenticates a person by automatically reading and matching fingerprints.
what: Apple introduced Touch ID fingerprint unlocking on the iPhone 5s, putting fingerprint readers in millions of ordinary phones.

sources.title: Touch ID
sources.quote: the iPhone 5s was unveiled on September 10, 2013, and was the first phone on a major US carrier to feature the technology.

note: Introduction year, not a measured adoption figure; use is routine on phones from about 2013 to 2015.

name: Retina and iris recognition
definition: A machine that identifies a person by scanning the patterns of the eye.
what: John Daugman patented and published the first working iris-recognition algorithms and gave the first live demonstrations.

sources.title: Iris recognition
sources.quote: In 1994 he patented this basis for iris recognition and its underlying computer vision algorithms for image processing

note: Flom and Safir's 1980s patent on the concept had no working algorithm, so rejected. Retina scanning is older: EyeDentify was formed in 1976 and a scanner concept emerged in 1975 (Retinal scan article), but I found no dated working demonstration, so no retina milestone is given.

name: Automated face recognition
definition: Cameras and computers that identify people by matching their faces against stored images.
what: The Mexican government used face recognition software to detect duplicate voter registrations for the 2000 presidential election.

sources.title: Facial recognition system
sources.quote: In the 2000 Mexican presidential election, the Mexican government employed face recognition software to prevent voter fraud.

note: The same article says West Virginia and New Mexico DMV offices were first to use it after 1993 (undated), so an earlier use likely exists. Super Bowl XXXV (2001) is later.

name: Automated face recognition
definition: Cameras and computers that identify people by matching their faces against stored images.
what: Apple announced Face ID on the iPhone X, bringing face recognition to ordinary phone unlocking.

sources.title: Face ID
sources.quote: Apple announced Face ID alongside the iPhone X on September 12, 2017

note: Introduction date, not a measured adoption figure.

name: Office automation
definition: Computers and machines that do clerical work such as correspondence, filing, billing and payroll.
what: LEO I at J. Lyons and Co. ran the first business application on a computer.

sources.title: LEO (computer)
sources.quote: LEO I ran its first business application in 1951.

note: Mechanical tabulators and accounting machines (from the 1890s) do clerical work; I treated the concept as electronic/computer clerical work and did not research them. Payroll dates (1951 vs 1953) conflict across sources.
